data.exact_reserve_text: During 2015 the estimated ultimate loss ratio (net of acquisitions costs) on certain lines of business for the 2014 and prior years of account was increased. These increases are set out in the table below together with their effect on ultimate claims reserves.

prior_year_events.impact_description: Worse than expected claims experienced primarily in the US liability account leading to significant reserve increases for 2013 and prior years of account.
Estimated ultimate loss ratio increased for Personal Accident & Sickness for 2014 and prior years, increasing claims reserves.
Estimated ultimate loss ratio increased for Special Lines for 2014 and prior years, increasing claims reserves.

data.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate strengthened prior years' gross claims reserves by GBP 35.757m in 2015, primarily reflecting adverse development in its US liability portfolio (the largest contributor), together with smaller reserve increases in Personal Accident & Sickness and Special Lines. Management attribute the movement to worse-than-expected claims development in volatility-prone liability exposures (including litigious jurisdictions and poorer-performing coverholders) and accordingly increased ultimate loss estimates for 2014 and earlier years.
raw_causal_phrases: During 2015 the estimated ultimate loss ratio (net of acquisitions costs) on certain lines of business for the 2014 and prior years of account was increased.
The result was affected by worse than expected claims experienced primarily in the US liability account which is no longer written in that form
exposures to more volatile sectors of industry in heavily litigious jurisdictions through poor coverholders has led to significant loss and reserve increases for the 2013 and prior years of account
reserves strengthened substantially for the 2013 and prior years of account

gross_premium_mix.line_of_business: Fire and other damage to property

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development figure derived from the 'Movement in prior year's provision for claims outstanding' note (table of increases by internal class) which reports gross increases in GBP 000; these have been summed and converted to millions. A gross claims development triangle is present and was cross-checked. No specific named catastrophe events were identified as drivers; the movement principally arises from adverse development in the US liability account. All source figures in the notes are presented in GBP 000 in the report and were converted to millions for this output.
